bpmn:participant.name: BPMN-15 | Scheduled Subscription Ingredient Reservation and Retry

bpmn:process.name: Scheduled Subscription Ingredient Reservation and Retry
bpmn:process.bpmn:documentation: Sources: docs/proposed-bpmn-catalog.md (all process boundaries reviewed); Chapters/Kitchen406 - Capstone Paper.md SRS 4.12 FR-INV-03-05,21-23, supporting FR-INV-19 and SRS 4.13 FR-BOM-07-08, NFR-REL-03,05. Implementation: index.html loads app/inventory-state.js (I.plan, I.available, I.reserve), app/staff-integration.js (B.reserveNext, stock-change retry), app/staff-state.js and app/owner-inventory.js. SRS governs timing: the preview reserves the next pending delivery and retimes later requirements relative to previous preparation; this model instead reserves each later fulfillment one calendar day before its own current preparation date (FR-INV-21). One instance per fulfillment and attempt. Two alternative system start events represent scheduled execution and automatic retry after separately recorded replenishment. FR-INV-23 allows retry but does not mandate manual initiation; automatic stock-change retry follows app/staff-integration.js S.changed. Authorized owner/staff restocking remains in BPMN-24, outside this process. One System swimlane represents the sole acting role. Both starts connect directly to Load as alternative entries (no synchronization or redundant merge gateway). Local validation and BoM calculation are shown directly on the main diagram. Visible rule annotations explain eligibility, calculation, availability and atomic commit decisions. Local validation and BoM calculation are shown directly on the main diagram. Visible rule annotations explain eligibility, calculation, availability and atomic commit decisions. No message flows are needed within the pool. This is descriptive BPMN, not an executable scheduler. Recheck the current date/version at dispatch and commit, including deferments from BPMN-06. No duplicate reservations, capacity booking, checkout hold, payment, consumption, automatic purchase, cancellation or deferment. Reservation timing remains FR-INV-21 pending separate resolution of the user-raised completion-trigger proposal. No other BPMN is changed.

bpmn:startEvent.name: One day before scheduled preparation
bpmn:startEvent.bpmn:documentation: FR-INV-21. Scheduler dispatches for a later paid subscription fulfillment using its current preparation date minus one calendar day in the business schedule timezone. Rescheduled records invalidate stale triggers.

bpmn:startEvent.name: Stock replenished for a failed reservation
bpmn:startEvent.bpmn:documentation: FR-INV-23. Automatic system retry after BPMN-24 — Ingredient Stock Restocking has separately saved an authorized restock. Start one attempt for each affected previously failed subscription reservation. Replenishment does not guarantee sufficient stock. The paper permits retries without specifying a manual initiator; automatic retry is supported by app/staff-integration.js S.changed. Owner/Staff authentication applies to the separate restocking action, not to an approval in this process.

bpmn:serviceTask.name: Load current subscription fulfillment and reservation state
bpmn:serviceTask.bpmn:documentation: Read confirmed paid subscription, later fulfillment identity, current preparation/reservation dates, material issue and existing ingredient reservation. First fulfillment retains checkout ingredients from BPMN-09/13, linked by BPMN-04. No rebooking of committed capacity.

bpmn:businessRuleTask.name: Check later fulfillment, due date and retry eligibility
bpmn:businessRuleTask.bpmn:documentation: Later, paid, confirmed, unprepared fulfillment; current scheduled due date reached. For the replenishment entry, require a recorded failed ingredient reservation and subsequent saved replenishment. Validate against the current agreed preparation date, including any permitted BPMN-06 deferment; do not reserve future weeks early. Stale schedule, first fulfillment or ineligible state cannot allocate stock. An existing complete reservation is safely reused by the next decision.

bpmn:exclusiveGateway.name: Eligible and due?
bpmn:exclusiveGateway.bpmn:documentation: Later, paid, confirmed, unprepared fulfillment; current scheduled due date reached. For the replenishment entry, require a recorded failed ingredient reservation and subsequent saved replenishment. Validate against the current agreed preparation date, including any permitted BPMN-06 deferment; do not reserve future weeks early. Stale schedule, first fulfillment or ineligible state cannot allocate stock. An existing complete reservation is safely reused by the next decision.

bpmn:serviceTask.name: Return ineligible / not-due reason; retain saved state
bpmn:serviceTask.bpmn:documentation: First fulfillment, unpaid/unconfirmed, already preparing/completed, stale schedule, future due date or retry without recorded failure/replenishment: no allocation. Preserve paid purchase and current schedule; a valid trigger may start a later attempt.

bpmn:endEvent.name: No reservation change
bpmn:endEvent.bpmn:documentation: Retain current state. A valid scheduled trigger or system retry after replenishment may start a new attempt. No payment, schedule or capacity change.

bpmn:exclusiveGateway.name: Complete active reservation exists?
bpmn:exclusiveGateway.bpmn:documentation: Existing complete active reservation for this fulfillment: reuse it without creating another. Recheck under the same per-fulfillment lock during save; concurrent attempts cannot both allocate.

bpmn:businessRuleTask.name: Calculate fulfillment ingredients using BPMN-26 BoM rules
bpmn:businessRuleTask.bpmn:documentation: FR-INV-03-05; FR-BOM-07-08. Refer to BPMN-26 — Fulfillment Material Requirements Projection: applicable recipe/variant quantities multiplied by each saved product-line quantity, summed per ingredient in compatible inventory units. Return ingredient requirements and any missing/invalid recipe/configuration issue. This is rule reuse, not invocation of an absent external process. No physical consumption or purchasing.

bpmn:serviceTask.name: Record recipe/data issue; preserve prior state
bpmn:serviceTask.bpmn:documentation: Missing or invalid recipe/ingredient data cannot be treated as zero requirements or a stock shortage. Record diagnosis and retain failed attempt for safe recovery; no new reservation or physical movement.

bpmn:serviceTask.name: Calculate available stock for every required ingredient
bpmn:serviceTask.bpmn:documentation: Available quantity = recorded physical stock minus other active ingredient reservations. Use consistent inventory units and validated requirement quantities. This fulfillment is excluded from other-reservation totals; a complete existing reservation is reused, never allocated again.

bpmn:serviceTask.name: Record missing ingredients and failed reservation
bpmn:serviceTask.bpmn:documentation: FR-INV-22-23. Save fulfillment-linked missing quantities/shortfall and recovery status. Preserve paid fulfillment, date and capacity. No physical movement or automatic cancellation. Do not overwrite a concurrent successful reservation with a stale shortage.

bpmn:intermediateThrowEvent.name: Publish owner shortage notification — BPMN-29
bpmn:intermediateThrowEvent.bpmn:documentation: FR-INV-22. Asynchronous handoff: Refer to BPMN-29 — Internal Notification Creation and Read Acknowledgment. Publish fulfillment/ingredient shortage and owner-recipient context after recording failure; that process owns notification creation/read state. No waiting for acknowledgement; notification failure does not change reservation result. External channel dispatch, when applicable, belongs to BPMN-28 and is not assumed here.

bpmn:endEvent.name: Shortage awaiting restocking and retry
bpmn:endEvent.bpmn:documentation: BPMN-24 records restocking separately. A fresh retry enters above and rechecks current stock; repeated shortage remains possible. No indefinite in-process polling or implicit success.

bpmn:serviceTask.name: Recheck current state; reserve all ingredients atomically
bpmn:serviceTask.bpmn:documentation: FR-INV-21,23; NFR-REL-03,05. Under serialized/version-checked update, recheck eligibility and existing reservation, compare all material requirements with physical stock minus other active reservations, and reserve every required ingredient together. Reservation is keyed by fulfillment identity. Repeated attempts reuse success; insufficient stock creates no partial reservation. Save reservation and clear its shortage status consistently. Physical stock is unchanged; BPMN-17 records actual consumption. Missing/invalid recipe or write failure is a technical issue, never a successful reservation or a stock-shortage assertion; retain prior state and log for safe retry.

bpmn:exclusiveGateway.name: Reservation commit outcome?
bpmn:exclusiveGateway.bpmn:documentation: Reserved includes a concurrent attempt whose complete reservation was safely reused. Distinguish actual shortage from configuration or save errors.

bpmn:endEvent.name: Ingredients reserved; shortage cleared
bpmn:endEvent.bpmn:documentation: Output: full active ingredient reservation linked to fulfillment, shortage cleared. Refer to BPMN-16 — Preparing-Owner Assignment and Allocation Validation and BPMN-17 — Fulfillment Preparation and Ready Confirmation as later processes; preparation still requires their controls.

bpmn:serviceTask.name: Log conflict/save failure; retain prior state for recovery
bpmn:serviceTask.bpmn:documentation: Invalid/missing recipe, stale write or persistence failure: no new partial allocation. Preserve prior saved state, record diagnosis and retain attempt for safe recovery. Retry cannot duplicate reservations.

bpmn:endEvent.name: No partial update; issue awaiting recovery

bpmn:textAnnotation.bpmn:text: Eligibility rules • Later paid, confirmed, unprepared fulfillment. • Current preparation date minus one day has arrived. • Respect a permitted BPMN-06 deferment. • Replenishment retry: prior failed reservation and saved restock. First ingredients already come from BPMN-09/13; capacity is already committed.

Refer to BPMN-26 — Material Requirements Projection Use each product variant’s applicable recipe × line quantity; sum by ingredient in matching units. Missing/invalid requirements cannot count as zero or as a successful reservation.
Available stock = physical stock − other active reservations. Every required ingredient must have enough available stock. Reservation is a commitment, not physical consumption.

Atomic commit rules Recheck current date/version and stock. Reuse an existing successful reservation. Reserve all ingredients together; clear shortage. On failure: no partial update. Physical stock is unchanged.
